![10 User Research Methods to Help You Design Better Product](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10081545-2633-0066-0000-d94c8907bf21:4)
User research methods are `techniques used to collect data about user needs, behaviors, and motivations to guide product design and development`.[[1]](https://enterprisearchitecture.harvard.edu/user-research-methods-and-recommendations)[[2]](https://www.leanlab.co/blog/a-simple-guide-to-user-research-methods-for-ux-designers)

### Core Dimensions of Research

- **Qualitative vs. Quantitative:** Qualitative research explores *why* users act or feel a certain way through small-sample observations and interviews. Quantitative research measures *how much* or *how many* using numerical data and large sample sizes.[[1]](https://maze.co/guides/ux-research/methods/)[[2]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/user-research-types)
- **Attitudinal vs. Behavioral:** Attitudinal research captures what users *say* they feel or think (via self-reported data like surveys). Behavioral research tracks what users *actually do* in practice (via interaction tracking and testing).[[1]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/research-methods-glossary/)[[2]](https://www.leanlab.co/blog/a-simple-guide-to-user-research-methods-for-ux-designers)
- **Generative vs. Evaluative:** Generative research happens early to find unmet needs and shape strategy. Evaluative research tests existing concepts or prototypes to check usability.[[1]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/)[[2]](https://www.leanlab.co/blog/a-simple-guide-to-user-research-methods-for-ux-designers)

### Key User Research Methods

- **User Interviews:** One-on-one conversations that reveal deep personal motivations, goals, and frustrations.
- **Usability Testing:** Observing users as they try to complete specific tasks on a design or product to find friction and usability flaws.
- **Surveys:** Structured questionnaires used to gather scalable attitudinal data and quantify user sentiment.
- **Card Sorting:** An exercise where users group information to help design intuitive [Information Architecture](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/).
- **Field Studies:** Observing users directly in their natural environment to understand real-world workflows and context.
- **A/B Testing:** Quantitative split testing that compares two product versions to see which performs better.[[1]](https://formbricks.com/blog/user-research-methods)[[2]](https://enterprisearchitecture.harvard.edu/user-research-methods-and-recommendations)[[3]](https://www.leanlab.co/blog/a-simple-guide-to-user-research-methods-for-ux-designers)[[4]](https://figr.design/blog/user-research-methods)[[5]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/research-methods-glossary/)[[6]](https://maze.co/guides/ux-research/methods/)

You can review a complete framework breakdown via the NN/G Guide to UX Research Methods.[[1]](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/which-ux-research-methods/)If you want to choose a method, tell me:

- What **phase** is your project in (early idea vs. ready to launch)?
- Are you trying to learn **what users say** or **what they do**?

I can help you pick the right technique.
